title: Paginated fanout patterns and graceful degradation for SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Product teams are asking for consistent, low-friction SDK behaviors when consuming list and streaming endpoints across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Current inconsistencies lead to developer confusion and subtle production bugs: different default retry windows, missing backpressure semantics for streaming, and divergent autopagination ergonomics (synchronous vs async). This ticket defines a single playbook for paginated fetchers, retry behavior during fanout/autopagination, and how streaming endpoints should surface backpressure and cancellation across language idioms.

Goals:
- Deliver language-parallel SDK primitives for pagination (page-level and item-level iteration), for streaming responses (chunked/stream events), and for safe autopagination with bounded parallelism.
- Define safe default retry/backoff policies for fetchable pages and streaming reconnects.
- Specify idempotency guidance and auto-instrumentation required for retries during autopagination/fanout.
- Provide acceptance criteria, design clarifications, and a rollout plan to implement in Python/TS/Go SDKs.

Non-goals:
- Automatic de-duplication of server-side items beyond basic client-side dedupe when page tokens are reused.
- Auto-retry of non-idempotent write operations (POST/PATCH) unless API exposes explicit idempotency token support.

Summary of recommended UX patterns (high-level):
1) Two surface primitives per list endpoint: pages() and items().
   - pages(): returns a lazy sequence/iterator of raw page objects (includes metadata: next_token, request_params, raw_count).
   - items(): flattens pages() into a lazy stream of individual items. Both should be available in sync and async forms as appropriate for the language.
2) Autopagination: an opt-in convenience that can run sequentially (default) or with bounded parallelism (concurrency parameter). When parallelism > 1, SDK must rate-limit in-flight page fetches to a safe default (4) and expose cancellation.
3) Fanout pattern: for endpoints that return per-shard cursors or allow partitioned fetches, SDK will expose a fanout helper that accepts a partitioning function and orchestrates bounded concurrent fetches with backpressure and aggregated error handling.
4) Streaming endpoints: provide an async iterator (TS/py) or channel-based reader (Go) that yields events/chunks and supports: explicit Cancel/Close; pull-based reading where applicable; reconnection/backoff policy for server-initiated disconnects (with max retry cap).

Retry and backoff model (defaults):
- Base backoff: 200ms; multiplier 2.0; jitter: full jitter; max backoff: 5s; max attempts: 5.
- Retryable conditions: network timeouts, 429, 502, 503, 504. 5xx otherwise (500) requires conservative handling: only retry when idempotency can be guaranteed or when operation is read-only.
- For autopagination parallel fetches, apply per-request retry limits but globally cap concurrent retries to avoid thundering herd.

Idempotency and safe retries:
- SDK will automatically attach an idempotency token (Idempotency-Key) header for autopagination or fanout operations that perform POST-style fetches, but only if the server advertises idempotency support via response headers or API schema.
- For plain GET list endpoints, retries are safe by default, but SDK must provide an option to enable strict de-duplication when page tokens are not stable.

Backpressure and cancellation:
- Streaming readers must implement a pull model where caller controls when next chunk is requested. SDK should not buffer arbitrarily large amounts of data.
- Provide a cancellation token / context pattern (context.Context in Go, CancellationToken in TS, context manager / asyncio.Task.cancel in Python examples) that stops in-flight work, clears buffers, and surfaces a CancellationError to the caller.

Observability and telemetry:
- Emit structured telemetry events for: page_fetch_start, page_fetch_success, page_fetch_retry, page_fetch_failure, stream_connected, stream_disconnected, stream_reconnect_attempt.
- Tag events with sdk_language, endpoint, api_version, pagination_mode (cursor/offset), concurrency, retries_used.

Compatibility and surface parity requirements across languages:
- All three SDKs must offer: pages(), items(), autopaginate(options), stream_reader() APIs with equivalent behavior documented. Language-idiomatic names allowed (e.g., iterate_pages / iterate_items in Go).
- Async vs sync: expose both sync and async surfaces where idiomatic (Python: sync + async; TS: promise + async iterator; Go: blocking iterator + channel-based stream).
- Error model: map transient errors to a shared typed RetryableError with language-specific wrappers. Permanent errors should carry raw HTTP status, body, and request id.
- Deprecation: any breaking changes to pagination tokens or stream framing must follow a 3-release deprecation window and provide a compatibility shim for older SDK versions when feasible.

Documentation and examples required: one-endpoint example demonstrating: manual pagination, autopagination sequential, autopagination parallel (N=4), streaming with cancellation, and handling rate-limited responses. Each example must exist in the language-specific README and in the central docs site.
acceptance_criteria: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs expose pages() and items() primitives for target list endpoints and match documented behavior.
Autopagination is opt-in; default runs sequentially; parallel autopagination is gated behind an explicit concurrency parameter and default cap of 4.
Retry/backoff defaults implemented and configurable; tests prove behavior against flaky test server (inject transient 502/503 and verify bounded retries).
Streaming readers implement pull semantics, support cancellation, and provide reconnection policy with an upper bound of reconnect attempts (5) before surfacing failure.
Telemetry events emitted for page_fetch_* and stream_* events and available in console traces for a test scenario.
API docs include code samples for manual paging, autopagination (seq + parallel), and streaming in all three languages.
Unit and integration tests added to each SDK repo; integration tests run in CI against a local flaky server harness; test matrix covers cursor and offset pagination modes.
Backcompat: existing public methods (if any) remain available; new methods are additive. Breaking changes must go through deprecation process specified in release notes.
scope:
In scope: GET/list endpoints (cursor and offset), server-initiated streaming endpoints (chunked/event stream), client-side autopagination helper and fanout helper, default retry/backoff config, telemetry hooks, cross-language documentation and examples.
Out of scope: automatic reconciliation of duplicated items across pages beyond simple client dedupe; autopagination for non-GET mutation endpoints unless server-idempotency is explicit.
open_questions: Which header should we standardize for next-token name (Next-Page-Token vs X-Next-Token) — do we require server change?
What HTTP error codes should we include/exclude from the default retry set for streaming reconnects?
Should autopagination parallel fetches be enabled by default behind a runtime flag for hosted users?
Contract for idempotency token auto-injection: will all server APIs advertise support via schema or header?
decisions: Autopagination will be opt-in by default; sequential mode is default when autopagination is enabled.
Default concurrency cap for parallel autopagination set to 4 to balance latency vs server pressure.
Use full jitter backoff with base 200ms, multiplier 2.0, max backoff 5s, max attempts 5 as default policy across SDKs.
SDKs will attach telemetry tags for retries and pagination_mode; console will ingest these for rollout analysis.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): land pages()/items() API in all SDKs as beta behind a feature flag; add unit tests and language-parity examples. Phase 2 (2 sprints): add autopagination helper, parallel fetch option, and fanout helper; enable telemetry events from SDKs. Phase 3 (1 sprint): streaming reader parity and reconnection semantics; run integration tests against flaky harness and gather performance telemetry. Phase 4: documentation publication, migration guide, and gradual enablement by default after internal dogfooding and metrics review.
notes: Related existing PRDs on streaming/pagination exist; this ticket synthesizes for a unified developer playbook focused on ergonomics and safe autopagination.
We should coordinate with infra on rate-limiting signals and add a server header to indicate recommended parallelism when available.
Design should include small helper for client-side dedupe (optional) when servers return unstable tokens.
